_about: Modules: what a machine wears inside, beside its die (bible section 10, the modules row). A chassis carries module_slots of them (two as a rule, three on the Clydesdale; a number of the chassis, never bought). A module is read like a passive: any number of stat lines (stats: the engine's stat names, hull, shield, heat, armour, move, cooling, shield_regen, added through Effects) beside at most one text (text: a description shown to the player and its effects, checked like a passive's; a text the engine cannot run carries "status": "planned"). Every module has a tier, 1 to 3, so the first battle offers plain ones; the capital's maker has no tier one. The archetypes (plate, kit, overload, prototype) are a design guide, never stored or checked. Shown: name, codex, flavour, the text's description; internal text under design.

design.fantasy: Bolt-on armour that comes off in sheets so the hull does not.
design.niche: A plate: plain stats, the starting module.

text.description: Its Direct blows aimed at the front rank deal 1 more.

design.fantasy: A reinforced prow and a driver who stopped asking.
design.niche: A reach read (Ryan, 22 October): +1 on Direct blows aimed at the front rank, the Artillery Rangefinder its mirror at the back for Indirect blows. Without a rule it measured the best module on every machine (the bible's catalogue row); its armour line went with the rule, and its stat line comes from the pricing run after the landing.

design.fantasy: The Honey Badger's old passive, Minerva's legendary frame: whatever breaks, it keeps working.
design.niche: Campaign insurance more than a fight effect (Ryan, 15 October: "Never destroyed - module, yes. Tier 2 or 3, not sure. Can have positive stats since that's not that impactful an effect"): tier two on Ryan's go of 31 October, the Ram Frame's hull line beside its rule.

text.description: Taking hull damage stands up 2 shield.

design.fantasy: A lining that catches what comes off the inside of the armour, and throws it back out as a wall.
design.niche: A prototype: a slower, hotter machine that never takes two bare-hull blows running.

text.description: Damage past a kill in the front rank spills into the foe behind, from any of its weapons.

design.fantasy: A drive train that never lets off: whatever falls in front of it, the push carries on into whatever stood behind.
design.niche: Ryan, 12 November: "Spillover can be a module." The Wild Boar's Juggernaut Drive gave Spillover to every weapon it fired until 11 November, when he retired it from the Boar as a sole mechanic ("Spillover as a sole mechanic is pretty lame. Not much to build around there"); worn by any machine, it is one rule among its kit's. A session's name, kept on his word of 12 November ("The working names are fine as are the placeholder numbers"); the hull line is the Ram Frame's placeholder until the pricing run.

text.description: Each time its heat climbs, it stands up 1 shield.

design.fantasy: Bleed air off the hot skin and blow it across the hull as a cushion.
design.niche: A kit: a small rule; a hot machine is a shielded one. Its point of cooling went on 19 November (Ryan's yes: cooling is a kit's or a locked piece's, never a slot's).

design.fantasy: Everything leaves the barrel faster. Including the barrel, eventually.
design.niche: The ceiling to the Tactical Databank's floor: a rolled weapon's highest roll raised a little.
design.notes: Awaits a rule since 2 November: rolled damage is gone (Ryan, decided in play testing: "I want rolled damage gone for sure"), so a ceiling or a floor has nothing to move. Its old rule: Its rolled weapons reach 1 higher.

text.description: Every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe runs twice as hot.

design.fantasy: Afterburners on the walk to the fight, and the fight paid for in heat.
design.niche: An overload: speed and shield for double heat; a perk on a machine that wants heat (the Buzzard).

design.fantasy: A little armour is better than the amount you had.
design.niche: A plate: plain stats, the starting module.

design.fantasy: Radiator grilles off a field kitchen, bolted wherever they fit.
design.niche: A plate for heat: a hotter machine. Its point of cooling went on 19 November (Ryan's yes: cooling is a kit's or a locked piece's, never a slot's); the maximum stays.

text.description: Its rolled weapons' lowest roll is 1 higher.

design.fantasy: Every firing solution the regiment ever logged, in a box that hums.
design.niche: The floor to the Muzzle Velocity Booster's ceiling: a rolled weapon's lowest roll raised a little.
design.notes: Awaits a rule since 2 November: rolled damage is gone (Ryan, decided in play testing: "I want rolled damage gone for sure"), so a ceiling or a floor has nothing to move. Its old rule: Its rolled weapons' lowest roll is 1 higher.

text.description: Its Indirect blows aimed at the back rank deal 1 more.

design.fantasy: A man with a theodolite who has never once been wrong about where a shell lands.
design.niche: The Ram Frame's mirror (Ryan, 22 October): a reach read, +1 on Indirect blows aimed at the back rank, where the Frame reads Direct blows at the front; its stat line comes from the pricing run after the landing.

text.description: An ally it shields is Armoured 1 for the round.

design.fantasy: The field it lends comes back mirrored, and the mirror holds.
design.niche: A kit for the support frame: a shield spent on an ally is armour too.

text.description: Its blows deal 1 more to a foe carrying any status.

design.fantasy: A matrix of how much each thing in front of it wants to fall apart.
design.niche: A kit: a status machine's payoff.

text.description: Every blow on it lands 2 harder.

design.fantasy: A shell of something with negative mass. Hits do not quite agree with it.
design.niche: An overload: a huge shield that every small hit chews into.

design.fantasy: Armour inscribed with the Arsenal's tolerances. It holds because it was told to.
design.niche: A plate, at tier two: the Arsenal fields no tier one.

text.description: Taking hull damage Empowers it, a stack a blow.

design.fantasy: It keeps a record of every wound, and it reads the list aloud.
design.niche: A kit: a machine that hits harder the more it is hit.

text.description: Every component it spends costs 3 hull.

design.fantasy: The machine takes its due before it does anything you ask.
design.niche: An overload: a great deal of hull and shield with a price on every action; a perk where the hull is already being spent (the Nemesis).

text.description: Rerolling only its own die is free once a round.

design.fantasy: Small hinged tabs on every control surface, trimmed in flight: the airframe settles onto whatever it was aiming for.
design.niche: The Kestrel line's reroll module: another look at its own die, a free reroll a round, paid in heat maximum so no module is the universal pick.

text.description: Doubles the number of hits for Weapons and Equipment. Base weapon damage is halved (rounded down, minimum 1).

design.fantasy: The Skua's first passive, a breech that cycles twice for every pull, as a part any machine can wear (Ryan, 12 November: "Turn the skua split strikes into a module").
design.niche: Count for magnitude: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe hits twice, each hit's base halved, rounded down and never below one, every buff and rider whole on each hit. The text is his of 7 November, less its clause for Sweep. Riders and flat buffs double on it, plate takes twice, and a weapon of 1 a strike is doubled outright (the Flechette Pod's four strikes become eight), the first thing to watch. Tier two and no stat line are placeholders; a second one adds nothing.
